description: USFS replaced its 9 regional offices with 15 state directors, many overseeing several states. Staff describe regional reporting chains as upended. The role now combines line authority with state-partnership brokering.

role_title: State forestry staff delivering federal land work under Good Neighbor Authority
description: States are being asked to help manage federal land as USFS capacity shrinks (about 16% of staff lost). State foresters report key vacancies and unclear expectations, which raises demand for federal process knowledge in state roles.

role_title: DOI bureau wildland fire positions (BIA, BLM, NPS, FWS, OAS, OWF) consolidated into USWFS
description: Fire programs from six DOI units were consolidated into the U.S. Wildland Fire Service (Jan 2026). Aligned USWFS/USFS qualification standards take effect Jan 2027, and some positions will be archived.

role_title: Fish and Wildlife Administration (0480), Zoology (0410), Horticulture (0437), Animal Science (0487) realigned to 0401
description: OPM Phase One consolidation realigns these low-employment series into General Natural Resources Management and Biological Science (0401). Grade and pay are unchanged, but duties must be described within 0401.

role_title: Range Technician (0455) to 0404; Outdoor Recreation Planning (0023) to 0186
description: OPM Phase One realigns 0455 (147 employees) into Biological Science Technician (0404) and 0023 (368) into 0186. Range-specific competencies risk losing visibility in a broader series.

role_title: Environmental Protection Assistant (0029) to 0303; Environmental Health Technician (0698) to 0640
description: OPM Phase One realigns these into general assistant and health technician series, removing environment-specific series identity at the support level.

role_title: Agency strategic hiring committee members and talent teams
description: EO 14356 (Oct 2025) requires strategic hiring committees to approve every vacancy and annual staffing plans aimed at critical skills gaps. The Merit Hiring Plan requires agency talent teams. These are new decision points where skills-gap evidence is used.

role_title: Agency job-analysis and technical-assessment specialist (serving natural-resource series)
description: Chance to Compete requires job-analysis-based technical assessments, with Natural Resources Management a Tier 2 group. OPM notes agencies may need training to run local job analyses. Demand rises for HR staff who can run SME-based job analysis for environmental series.

The 2025 hiring freeze and 1-for-4 replacement order, a 12% fall in the federal civilian workforce (Sep 2024 to Jan 2026) and USFS losses narrow federal entry. This compounds v1's career-ladder-destruction concern.

role_title: Conservation corps members funded through AmeriCorps
description: Mass grant terminations in spring 2025 were partly restored by litigation. A Sep 2026 settlement protects FY2026, but the stay ends Feb 1, 2027. Land trusts report placements in jeopardy.

role_title: Forest Service research station scientists and technicians
description: The USFS reorganization keeps 20 research stations open and closes 57, removing a long-standing entry and development path for research technicians and field scientists.

The Corps Network's workforce team now focuses on career pathways, employer partnerships, credentialing, apprenticeships and post-placement outcomes, with a JFF practice framework. Corps staff roles are shifting from crew supervision toward career navigation.

Comment intake, binning and summarization are now tool-assisted in production (FWS DocketScope deployed 2025-08, analyst-verified) and in pilots at EPA Region 8, USDA OCIO and BLM (GraphRAG). Work shifts from coding comments to validating machine coding and tracing responses. DOI's PCAT was retired between inventories, so tools churn faster than the role.

role_title: Entry-level comment and document reviewers (GS-5/7 equivalents)
description: If first-pass coding is automated, the tasks through which juniors learned issue-spotting and regulatory reasoning shrink. No staffing data seen to confirm this; consistent with v1 CLD logic.

role_title: Interdisciplinary (ID) team members and planners in forest planning and NEPA
description: USFS deployed 'Forest Plan review and planning support' (Google, 2025-06) and 'Turbo plan' (Wildfire.org, 2025-07); BLM is building NEPA CE document generation and a small language model to consolidate RMP decisions. Planners increasingly review machine-drafted or machine-extracted content.

role_title: Camera-trap image tagger / wildlife technician (image review)
description: Pre-trained detectors and classifiers (MegaDetector + SpeciesNet) are used by Michigan DNR Wildlife Division, TNC California and others; NOAA automates seal, sea lion, whale and fish image counting. Manual image sorting - a traditional seasonal-technician entry task - is being compressed to exception review.
NOAA lists ML to automate review of EM data (Hawaii longline, shrimp, reef fish) and bycatch image libraries. Reviewer role shifts to validating detections and maintaining training libraries.

USGS bat-acoustics ML pilot; NOAA passive acoustic ML for marine mammals; BirdNET exposes train/evaluate commands to non-programmers. Value moves from manual call ID to detection-threshold setting, validation and occupancy inference.

role_title: Remote-sensing compliance analyst for farm programs
description: USDA Farm Production and Conservation is preparing satellite-and-crop-model verification of cover crops and planting dates and validation of acreage/crop type - the only environmental high-impact AI uses in its 2025 inventory. Requires model-risk, validation and appeal-support skills; may change the role of field spot checks (FC to assess).

role_title: Operational forecaster / environmental modeler working with AI emulators
description: NOAA inventory includes an AI-driven global forecast model and ensemble, the Ai2 Climate Emulator collaboration, AI downscaling and bias correction, and hybrid physics-ML models. Modelers must evaluate emulators against physics models and observations.

role_title: Fire intelligence and decision-support specialists (FBAN, LTAN, GISS, IRIN, UAS Data Specialist, Intelligence Support Specialist)
description: Incident analytic roles, coordination-center intelligence and new technology-integration roles (AI detection, camera networks, satellite tasking, data pipelines) are converging faster than NWCG qualifications and OPM series absorb them; classification spans GS-1560/2210/0132/0401.

role_title: Chief AI Officer staff and AI governance board members in environmental agencies
description: M-25-21 required CAIOs within 60 days and AI governance boards (with data representation) at CFO Act agencies; EPA places AI governance in its Data Governance Advisory Committee. Creates demand for staff who can make high-impact determinations and run inventories.

Agency AI strategies recruit for model evaluation and AI ethics roles (per DC-020); M-25-22 requires ongoing performance monitoring in contracts; no environmental-agency position descriptions for this role were found this session.

role_title: GIS technician (layer creation and map production)
description: v1 codes 2.1.1 T1 as CLD-Moderate. Inventory shows generative tools writing ArcGIS scripts and AI assistants inside Esri tools (pilots). Direct evidence of reduced GIS-technician hiring was not found; LM to test with posting data.

USDA NRCS DS Hub is piloting generative metadata for geospatial datasets; v1 codes 2.2.5 T3 as V (pipeline is primary executor). Work shifts from authoring to reviewing machine-generated metadata and sensitivity screening.

NOAA AI QC of water-level and ocean observations, IOOS coastal modeling sandbox, edge-AI survey payloads; USGS/USDA sensor QC. A distinct engineering role between field technicians and analysts, poorly captured by v1.

role_title: Environmental permit processor and applicant-assistance staff
description: USDA OCIO pilots AI triage predicting whether an application is a simple categorical exclusion; FWS is preparing ePermits chatbots and an application wizard. Routine routing compresses; exception handling and applicant guidance remain.

role_title: Environmental data scientist in science bureaus (USGS, NOAA, USFS R&D)
description: USGS alone reports 187 AI use cases (of DOI's 247) and NOAA 157 names; the work is mostly classical ML on Earth observation, hydrology, hazards and species data, increasingly with foundation models. Role shifts from building bespoke models to adapting, validating and operating shared models.

Operator work shifts from manual rounds, grab sampling and hand control toward supervising SCADA/advanced process control, alarm management and data review; OT cybersecurity becomes part of the job. Licensing (operator in responsible charge) keeps legal accountability with a human.

Certification grades require documented operating experience; automation that removes hands-on tasks (rounds, manual tests) may lengthen or hollow out the experience that certification is meant to certify. Same mechanism as v1 CLD but legally coupled to licensure.

Small systems rely on shared or remote operators and technical-assistance providers; remote monitoring extends coverage but concentrates accountability in fewer certified people. Confirm with ASDWA/NRWA data.

role_title: Lead service line inventory and replacement specialist
description: Inventory, predictive identification of unknown service lines, customer engagement and replacement program management emerged with lead and copper rule revisions and federal funding; timelines subject to 2025-26 rule changes.
AI-vision robotic sorters are deployed at materials recovery facilities, displacing manual pre-sort and QC sort positions while adding robot maintenance technician roles.

role_title: State/local recycling coordinator -> EPR program manager
description: State packaging EPR laws move public waste staff from running drop-off/education programs to overseeing producer responsibility organizations, needs assessments and performance audits.

role_title: Air monitoring technician -> sensor network/data QA technician
description: Low-cost sensor networks and satellite products add collocation, correction and data-fusion work alongside regulatory FRM/FEM operation; durable skill is judging data fitness for regulatory vs community use.

Emissions calculations, applicability screening and boilerplate permit drafting are candidates for AI assistance; judgment on applicability, enforceability and public process remains. No sector-specific evidence yet.

Targeting by e-reporting analytics, continuous and remote monitoring shifts inspectors from routine coverage to evidence-grade follow-up on flagged sources; fiscal pressure reduces inspection headcount.

Historical records review, database report interpretation and report drafting are the training ground for junior remediation staff and are highly compressible by AI; site reconnaissance and interviews are not.

Work moves from scheduled walk-down OGI surveys to responding to continuous-monitor and satellite alerts and verifying repairs; federal rule changes create demand volatility while state programs persist (verify).

role_title: Orphan well plugging program manager / crew
description: IIJA funding created state orphan-well programs and contractor demand; duration tied to appropriations (verify current status).
IIJA abandoned mine land funding expanded state and Tribal AML programs (project design, contract oversight, AMD treatment); verify program staffing trends.
2025 federal incentive phase-downs and federal-land permitting shifts move demand toward state siting processes and storage/transmission; consultants report volatility (verify with PS and USEER).

role_title: Utility vegetation management / wildfire mitigation specialist
description: Utility wildfire mitigation plans created roles combining arboriculture, fire risk modeling and LiDAR/satellite encroachment analytics.

Reporting work splits into (a) sustainability controller/assurance-readiness roles near finance and (b) strategy/transition-plan roles; AI compresses drafting. US federal retreat vs EU/California/ISSB adoption creates multi-regime work.
Limited and reasonable assurance requirements (e.g., California SB 253; EU) increase demand for verifiers with GHG and controls competence.
Integrity labels and third-party ratings created analyst roles evaluating additionality, permanence and MRV quality.

role_title: Chief heat officer / heat resilience coordinator
description: Some cities and counties created dedicated heat roles combining EM, public health and urban forestry.
Federal emergency management restructuring in 2025-26 shifts planning, recovery and mitigation work toward states and localities (verify scope with FEMA sources).
Disaster-driven, intermittent environmental review workforce; NEPA framework changes and AI review tools may compress review times; volatility in federal disaster staffing.
Degree and registration requirements narrow entry while climate (heat, vectors, HABs) adds workload; NEHA workforce assessments report recruitment difficulty (verify).
Sample-prep automation and LIMS shift analysts toward instrument QA and data validation; PFAS methods add capacity demand.
LiDAR and predictive site models change survey design and AI drafting compresses report writing - both are entry-level learning tasks; fieldwork judgment and consultation remain human.
NEPA page/time limits and the 2025 federal NEPA framework changes shift effort from long documents to scoping, commitment tracking and defensible concise analysis (SC to confirm current state).

With federal program capacity reduced in 2025-26, states carry more permitting, monitoring and enforcement load with flat or reduced budgets - pressure toward cross-media generalists and data-targeted work.
Federal research capacity was restructured in 2025 (e.g., EPA research office reorganization) with staff reductions; academic and state labs partially absorb functions (verify).

Park rangers fell 34.1% between Sep 2024 and Jan 2026, the steepest decline among environmental occupations in OPM-based data; interpretation and visitor protection shift to volunteers and seasonal staff.

role_title: Biological Science Student Trainee (GS-0499) and other Pathways trainees
description: Student trainee occupations decreased significantly and the under-30 share fell to 7.9% (Jan 2026); probationary firings in Feb 2025 removed early-career trail crews, biologists and NEPA coordinators.

Wildland fire management headcount rose while most environmental occupations fell; USFS had 10,496 firefighters on board in May 2026 against an 11,300 goal; DOI is consolidating bureau fire programs in phases. Year-round fuels and prescribed fire work expands the role beyond suppression.
About 1,600 Forest Service employees with fire certifications departed by May 2025; ~10,000 non-fire USFS staff hold fire qualifications. Surge capacity now depends on a smaller collateral-duty pool.
OPM Phase One proposes realigning 0455 into 0404; work continues under a broader technician series, so EMST role profiles must carry the function rather than the series.

role_title: Zoology (0410), Horticulture (0437), Fish & Wildlife Administration (0480), Animal Science (0487) -> 0401
description: Four small professional series proposed for realignment into 0401, broadening the catch-all series and increasing the need for competency profiles within it.
Both proposed for realignment out of named series (0023 to an 01xx series; 0090 to 1001). Recreation planning remains a function in USFS/NPS/BLM/USACE.

role_title: Environmental Protection Assistant (0029), Sanitarian (0688), Environmental Health Technician (0698)
description: Paraprofessional and environmental-health series proposed for realignment into generic series (0303, 0601, 0640), removing named entry points for environmental compliance and health work.

role_title: Land Law Examining (0965), Geodesy (1372), Geodetic Technician (1374), Forest Products Technology (1380), Irrigation System Operation (0459)
description: Proposed realignments to 0901, 1301, 1311 and a trades family; specialized lands, geodetic and forest-products work continues inside broader series.

role_title: Senior environmental policy, legal and program managers (GS-15+)
description: ~8,000 employees in ~4,800 positions moved to Schedule Policy/Career (97% GS-15+), including 98 EPA legal staff; these roles become at-will while remaining career, changing the integrity context for statecraft.

role_title: Agency talent team members and SME-assessors
description: Talent teams expanded to 154 agencies with 1,000+ members; SME-QA train-the-trainer certified 53 master trainers. Technical staff now co-produce hiring assessments.

v1 exposure tags code 6 of 7 entry-level (P) tasks under 0028 core competencies as compressive/substitution/supervision, the highest of 13 series; with AI-assisted drafting normalizing, entry work shifts from drafting to verification.
USFS lost about a quarter of its non-fire workforce by May 2025 and told Congress it needs state and community partners; remaining staff shift toward agreement management and partner oversight.
Dispatch-center staffing fell 25-27% in Colorado and Nevada per a county staffing study; dispatch data-entry tasks are automatable but error-sensitive.

Core competency set is datacraft-dominant (7 of 8 core competencies DC primary) and 50% of entry tasks are coded compressive; the role is migrating toward model/data review and toward overlap with 1560 data science.

USFS hired no non-fire seasonals in 2025 (budget) and committed to 2,000 seasonals for 2026, all titled forestry technician; district examples: Jackson RD 15 (2024) to 5 (2026), Teton Basin 9 to 2; application window ~10 days vs a normal Dec opening.

No temporary seasonal trail crews or wilderness rangers hired in 2025; trail miles maintained fell 22%; agency reports loss of equipment operation, rock masonry, volunteer coordination and project management skills and "backcountry trails are being abandoned".

April 2025 cuts of ~$400M to >1,000 AmeriCorps programs terminated or shrank corps (e.g., Lakes Region CC terminated; WisCorps -33%); PCT corps hours ~19,000 to ~4,000 expected. Some corps (Montana CC) kept funding.

~3,400 USFS probationary employees fired Feb 2025 (later litigation/reinstatement not tracked here) across trails, timber and watershed restoration; local reporting notes probationary staff are more likely to do field work; ~5,000 further voluntary departures; USFS lost about a quarter of its non-fire workforce.

Up to 1,400 red-card-qualified non-fire staff left in 2025; USFS asked deferred-resignation employees to return for fire season. Field qualifications held by non-fire staff are an uncounted surge capacity that shrinks when non-fire field roles shrink.

role_title: Collateral-duty UAS remote pilot (field specialist who also flies)
description: USFS: 371 pilots, 99% collateral duty; FY24 flights roughly +70% and hours +78% over FY23; 29% of hours on natural-resource missions; 73% of pilots current. Drone flying is being absorbed into existing field roles rather than creating a separate data role.
New NWCG-trained position under the firing boss; USFS aerial ignition by UAS treated 188,986 acres in FY24 and has been replacing helicopters for ignition; training takes 1.5-3 years.

Ignition shifting from helicopters to UAS; but policy shocks reverse it (DOI shifted some ignition back to helicopters when drones were restricted). Role persists as fallback; skills must be kept current on both platforms.

Part 108 (final rule at OIRA July 2026; publication status after that not verified) places accountability on operator organizations, requires organizational training programs and defines supervisory roles that can oversee multiple aircraft. Field drone work moves from one-pilot-one-aircraft to supervising fleets.

After the 2019-20 grounding BLM flights fell 3,643 to 528 and USGS 3,170 to 1,649 (2019-2023); compliant aircraft cost far more; pilot numbers fell; some surveys reverted to on-foot crews covering smaller areas. ASDA restrictions from Dec 2025 and the Dec 2025 FCC action continue to gate fleets. Adoption is policy-limited, not technology-limited.

role_title: State and local public-safety and resource drone operators
description: Dec 2025 FCC Covered List action is forward-looking but restricts new foreign models; NASAO-compiled figures: 25 states reported 467 restricted drones and up to $2B national exposure; Aug 2026 FCC proposal could extend to already-authorized thermal, LiDAR and ag-spray drones.

role_title: Wildlife survey technician (call-back and point-count surveys)
description: Where passive acoustic monitoring scales (e.g., northern spotted owl monitoring), survey work splits into recorder deployment/maintenance (field) and AI-assisted detection review (screen, field-formed expertise); fewer night call-back visits.
AI triage removes most blank-image sorting; remaining work is deployment design, servicing, theft/damage management and expert verification of species calls.

Continuous sondes and telemetry reduce routine grab-sample visits; visits become instrument service, calibration, fouling management and QC sampling. Emerging contaminants (PFAS) raise clean-sampling demands.
Lidar and imagery-based inventory reduce plot counts per estimate; remaining plots carry calibration weight and need tighter QA; cruisers move toward validating remote estimates.
Remote-sensing vendors, utilities and agencies need field reference data to validate products; currently done ad hoc by field staff or interns. Candidate structured learning role.

role_title: Utility vegetation management inspector / utility forester
description: Satellite and lidar risk scoring prioritizes spans; inspectors increasingly verify and override model scores in the field; wildfire mitigation plans expand the workforce.
Remote sensing, drones and analytics target inspections; fewer routine visits, more targeted and evidence-intensive visits. Not represented in v1.
Smaller crews, more lone work, more equipment and data-system supervision, and a heavier coaching load as entry hires fall; crew leads are where tacit transfer happens or fails.

role_title: Partner/NGO and contractor field crews filling agency gaps
description: USFS testimony: "We're going to need a lot of help from our state partners, our community partners"; Friends groups hiring their own seasonals (e.g., 17-18 for Bridger-Teton). Field work and its learning shift to partners whose crews are not in federal qualification records.

Seed- and seedling-dispensing drones are marketed for post-fire reforestation; field evidence on establishment rates was not verified. Planting crews unlikely to disappear within 5 years in steep, rocky or competing-vegetation sites.

role_title: Federal entry-level land-management technicians and student trainees (GS-0462/0404/0499)
description: 2025 hiring freeze, probationary firings and no non-fire seasonal hiring cut the federal entry rung; 2,000 seasonals restored in 2026; under-30 share 7.9%; student trainee occupations down. Driver is fiscal/policy, not AI; v1 CLD logic attributes ladder risk to automation only

role_title: Early-career analysts in high-LLM-exposure environmental occupations (environmental specialists, planners, compliance and sustainability analysts)
description: Env analytical occupations sit at the 90th-99th exposure percentile; private payroll evidence shows 22-25-year-olds in top-exposure quintiles ~19% below counterfactual by June 2026 via reduced hiring. No environment-specific employment evidence exists yet; ADP undercovers government

role_title: Environmental review and NEPA document specialists
description: Enterprise genAI drafting/summarizing tools are available near agency-wide at EPA (10,000-50,000 users) and DOI/USDA (50,000+ for some tools) while custom NEPA/permitting AI remains pilot or pre-deployment (5 cases, 0 deployed). NEPA procedure changes (SC) shorten documents and timelines. Task compression is plausible; staffing effect unobserved

role_title: Wildland fire operations and management positions
description: DOI fire programs consolidated into the U.S. Wildland Fire Service (Jan 2026) with aligned USWFS/USFS qualification standards due Jan 2027; wildland fire management series grew while other land-management occupations fell

role_title: Forest plan monitoring coordinators and resource data stewards
description: 2012-rule plans devote 22% of components to monitoring (median 34 per plan) vs 1.8% in 1982-rule plans; 1,506 monitoring questions across 45 plans; reporting/data-system language is the most-named method (16% of questions). Demand is for indicator design, evaluation reporting and data stewardship rather than for specific field methods

role_title: Partnership, cross-boundary and Tribal coordination roles
description: Per 1,000 components, 2012-rule plans name partnership touchpoints 31.4 vs 10.0 (1982 rule), Tribal 27.3 vs 10.0, cross-boundary 13.8 vs 4.5; USFS reorganization expands states' role (via AS). GNA/shared stewardship rarely appear in plan text (21 components) because they operate through agreements

role_title: Geospatial, remote-sensing and environmental data analysts in science bureaus
description: Of 504 AI use cases in environmental bureaus, 232 are classical ML; remote sensing/imagery (63; 11 deployed), species detection (89; 11 deployed) and hydrology (36; 10 deployed) dominate. AI is entering the analysis pipeline, mostly pre-deployment/pilot

role_title: Field survey biologists and technicians (species and habitat surveys)
description: Sensor-based detection (acoustic, camera, eDNA, imagery) is the main technology vector for field surveys, but plans rarely name methods (remote sensing in 3 monitoring questions, eDNA in 3). Method change will appear in protocols, PDs and postings, not plans; no index measures this sensing-substitution vector

role_title: Corporate sustainability and GHG/ESG reporting analysts
description: Sustainability Specialists are at the 97th exposure percentile; large-firm functions report growth (46%) more than cuts (25%) and higher compliance priority. Disclosure-rule volatility, not AI, is the dominant short-run driver

role_title: Senior scientific and technical staff in regulatory agencies (EPA and similar)
description: EPA staffing at 40-year lows; departing staff median tenure ~30 years vs ~11 years for those remaining (via FS). This removes the top of the ladder - the reviewers who certify AI-compressed work - a CLD mechanism v1 does not model
Park rangers -34.1% (via PPS/FH). v1 records a High CLD on 5.5.1 T1 (visitor services) attributed to AI compression; the observed decline is fiscal/policy-driven

Recreation is the largest theme in plan standards (3,819 components, 15%) and monitoring questions (17%); ROS and scenery classifications appear in 62 and 68 plans; special-use authorizations 363 touchpoints. v1 has no recreation planning or travel management competency

Lowest usage-based AI applicability of any env occupation (0.6th pct) and 75% physical tasks; change vector is SCADA/automation and cybersecurity, not LLMs; v1 has no water-utility competencies (audit)

LiDAR and modelled inventory compress the field-cruising hours through which junior foresters built stand-reading judgment; v1 prototype calls for calibration assignments and structured mentorship. Needs FC/LM corroboration with posting or staffing data.

Work shifts from first-draft writing toward screening, validating AI-drafted sections, data-standard compliance and administrative-record defensibility; federal action plan requires automated screening and GIS tools; public benchmark of AI drafting across 19 agencies; reported savings of 1-5 hours per subsection (vendor estimate).

role_title: Wildland fire intelligence and data analyst
description: DOI's SO 3448 directs an integrated wildland fire intelligence and data capability in the new USWFS; existing NWCG positions are incident-bound and no accredited fire-intelligence pipeline exists.
Operators increasingly run processes from sensor and control-system data; apprenticeship and mentor programs are expanding with EPA funding, but EMST has no treatment-operations competency.

Performance-based formation depends on qualified evaluators and mentors at the moment public-land agency staffing fell by double-digit percentages in several western states (reported); evaluator capacity, not course seats, may become the binding constraint on pathways.

role_title: Federal biologists moving to state agencies and consulting
description: Federal staffing reductions push experienced biologists toward state and consulting roles, where business development, applicant-side permitting and mitigation-market skills are needed (LC-PW-04). Flow data not found; CM to test with career histories.
Training staff will need to design AI-assisted practice and assessment while protecting formation; no environmental-sector evidence found this session.

role_title: Non-fire seasonal field technician (forestry, recreation, trails, wildlife)
description: No non-fire seasonal hiring at USFS in 2025; 2,000 seasonals committed for 2026, all titled forestry technician, with short application windows. The classic first rung into field craft was closed for a season and reopened narrower

Trail miles maintained fell 22% in 2025, with named tacit skills lost (equipment operation, rock masonry) and no seasonal trail crews. Corps hours on the PCT fell from ~19,000 to ~4,000. Skills reproduced only by crew apprenticeship are lost in one or two seasons

role_title: Conservation corps member -> agency technician pathway
description: $400M AmeriCorps cuts and terminations in 2025; FY2026 status litigated with a stay to 2027-02-01. No published alumni outcome data found. Whether noncompetitive hiring eligibility for corps service remains usable is unverified

Federal under-30 share fell to 7.9% (Jan 2026) from 8.9% (Sep 2024), against 19.4% of the US labour force. Student-trainee occupations declined (as recorded by FH). Accessions were 122,598 vs ~250,000 typical. Federal entry for new graduates is severely narrowed

NPS lost more than a quarter of its employees; park rangers down 34.1% (PPS figures as recorded by FH). v1 rates visitor-services entry work as High CLD (kiosks, chatbots), so entry is squeezed from both sides

role_title: Collateral-duty red-card holder (non-fire staff with fire quals)
description: ~1,400-1,600 fire-qualified non-fire staff departed. USFS relies on ~10,000 non-fire staff with fire quals and asked resigned workers to return. Surge fire capacity built through collateral duty is eroding as non-fire field staff shrink

DOI consolidated bureau fire programmes into the US Wildland Fire Service (Jan 2026). USWFS/USFS qualification standards align from Jan 2027. Intra-federal fire mobility should become easier; mobility to state, Tribal and contract fire depends on NWCG portability, which already exists

v1 rates four Domain 6 entry tasks as Substitution at the primary-learning position (regulatory research synthesis; compliance drafting; policy research; comment triage). Statecraft-primary competencies carry CLD flags at 37% vs 20-22% for FC/DC. No environment-specific external corroboration yet (LM's lane)

role_title: Entry-level project, budget and grants assistant
description: The most portable foundation competencies in v1 (3.1.1 project planning; 3.1.2 budget; Supporting in 10 families, Core in none) carry CLD flags; 3.1.2 is High severity. The skills that move people between actors are learned in entry tasks AI is compressing

role_title: Federal NEPA coordinator / biologist / planner moving to state or local government
description: Probationary firings hit NEPA coordinators and biologists. States ran programmes to recruit displaced federal staff, and a partnership formed to place them in state and local government. USFS turned to state and community partners for work. Federal-specific statecraft must be re-enacted under state law (SC enactment question)

role_title: County / state-park recreation-site manager taking over federal sites
description: Pitkin County will manage the Maroon Bells Scenic Area from 2027 under a USFS special use permit. Sweetwater Lake went to Colorado Parks and Wildlife in 2024. Federal functions are devolving to counties and states, creating roles that need federal-site knowledge plus local statecraft

role_title: Senior federal policy, legal and science staff in Schedule Policy/Career
description: ~8,000 positions (97% GS-15+) moved into Schedule Policy/Career, including EPA legal staff (as recorded by FH). Changed tenure and accountability may push experienced statecraft holders to states, NGOs or private employers. The mobility effect is not yet evidenced

Colorado and Maryland froze state hiring in summer 2025 even as states courted displaced federal staff. Displaced federal applicants (many with degrees) compete for the same entry and mid-level openings, and degree filters may return
v1 rates collecting ESG/GHG data for sustainability reporting (3.6.2 T1) as High CLD: AI accounting tools compress a new field's primary literacy-building task

At least 26 states have dropped or reduced degree requirements. In Pennsylvania ~60% of new hires lack a degree after 92% of positions were de-degreed. In Colorado the share of hires without a degree was flat at 25% (2023-24). Competency-based minimum qualifications are spreading, but conversion to hires depends on assessments and manager practice

Under the Chance to Compete Act, self-assessment questionnaires are phased out. USA Hire expands from 138 to 412 series, and 34.3% of delegated-examining announcements used technical assessments in FY26 Q2 (as recorded by FH). Assessed skills, not self-ratings, become the federal gate: the point where a portable competency language can matter
Controller-style roles that apply financial-reporting controls to sustainability data; present at more than half of Fortune 100 companies (2024).
Teams moving into legal and finance (teams reporting to legal doubled in two years); 2026: 58% raised compliance priority while 63% scaled back external communications.
63% of large-company respondents scaled back or rethought external sustainability communications; 16% weakened or abandoned targets.
Data collection and framework mapping are the automation target; vendors pitch software as a substitute for interns and consultants; v1 flagged 3.6.2 T1 Ac/P with career-ladder destruction.
Reported 12-18% pay premium for carbon accounting and Scope 3 skills; demand anchored by California SB 253 (Scope 3 from 2027) and ISSB adoption.
US demand driven by California limited assurance (2026) moving to reasonable (2030); EU dropped its planned reasonable-assurance step; CARB has not yet fixed provider qualifications.

EU scope cut roughly 90% (to >1,000 employees and >EUR450M turnover); revised ESRS simplify double materiality; demand concentrates in the largest EU and US multinationals and in consultants serving them.
SEC rules never took effect; rescission proposed 29 May 2026; preparation work for them has no regulatory anchor.
After record 2022-24 pay growth, 2026 survey reports slower US compensation growth and slightly lower senior pay.

Juniors learn by drafting sections, compiling tables and producing figures - the tasks most compressible by AI; firms may hire fewer juniors per project manager and create a reviewer shortage in 5-8 years.
Field sampling, monitoring and protocol surveys stay human and become the dominant entry path as desk drafting compresses; seasonal and lower paid.
Time-and-materials billing monetizes hours; AI-compressed drafting pushes firms toward fixed-fee or value pricing or margin compression.

role_title: Utility Wildfire Mitigation Analyst / Program Manager
description: Wildfire mitigation planning, public-safety power shutoff decisions and ignition-risk modeling became a distinct utility function, spreading across western utilities.
LiDAR, satellite and AI prioritization reduce routine patrols and shift work to validating model-flagged risks; still a major entry path for forestry graduates.
Hiring is volatile with 2025 federal tax-credit and federal-land approval changes; state permitting and transmission work may absorb some demand.
Role splitting into origination/landowner engagement, methodology/integrity science and dMRV engineering as integrity scrutiny and remote sensing mature.
Remote-sensing and ML scientists quantify carbon/nature outcomes for developers, raters and buyers; ground-truth and uncertainty design are the durable skills.
State producer-responsibility and chemical reporting laws create compliance roles distinct from voluntary circular-economy strategy.
Records review and report writing are highly automatable; fee-compressed product; site visit and environmental-professional judgment remain.
EHS software vendors are embedding AI (NAEM 2026 benchmark sponsored by them); compliance tracking and incident analytics augmented; certifying-official accountability unchanged.

role_title: Former federal environmental staff entering consulting/contracting
description: Movement of 2025-26 separated federal staff into private consulting and contracting is plausible but was not evidenced in this session; BLS medians imply many such moves are pay cuts for science roles. CM/LM should test with career-transition data.
ISSB plans a nature-related draft practice statement by Oct 2026; creates a corporate landing spot for ecologists.

NY DEC has a Climate Policy Analyst 1/2 title series that appears in DEC's title list and in the EPS 2 lateral-transfer list, so climate policy is now a formal civil-service occupation with its own ladder.

role_title: Former federal environmental staff entering state service
description: PA hired 1,350 people with federal experience by 2026-08 under an equivalency order; NY hired 28 in the first month of its campaign. No source breaks out environmental hires, and targeted roles skew to HR, IT, health and engineering.

role_title: State HR classification analyst using generative AI to crosswalk titles
description: PA HR staff used generative AI to match state qualifications to federal titles; MI runs an AI job-matching portal.

Permit drafting (fact sheets, standard conditions, deficiency letters) is highly codified and likely compressible by AI drafting, while limit derivation, defensibility and negotiation stay human. Postings show the task bundle; exposure is judged, not measured.

EGLE and MPCA run dedicated enforcement sections and unit supervisors who take escalated cases from district inspectors through settlement or litigation: inspection and case management are separating.

role_title: Entry-level environmental professional without a degree
description: Colorado reports 25% of 2024 hires in skills-emphasizing classes had no degree (1,588); MN MPCA supervisory classes are experience-only; FL ES II accepts 4 years' experience. CA, MI and TPWD classes still require degrees, so entry paths diverge by state.

role_title: Sub-licensure technical roles (Engineering Specialist, Geologic Specialist, Environmental Specialist)
description: Licensure statutes split classes into licensed and sub-licensure tracks (TX Engineering Specialist cannot perform PE duties; Geologic Specialist works under a licensed P.G.; WI renamed engineering-specialist classes under 2017 Act 111).

role_title: State DOT environmental scientist under dual CEQA/NEPA regime
description: Caltrans environmental scientists prepare both CEQA and NEPA documents subject to FHWA review, merging state and federal environmental review in one role.

role_title: Municipal environmental services specialist (science plus policy)
description: San Jose's class bundles environmental program management with contract, legislative advocacy and policy work, which v1 splits across domains 3, 5 and 6.
Operator retirements and automation of process control are widely reported pressures on utility staffing. Not evidenced this session; LM/DB to verify with AWWA, EPA or ASDWA data.
Registration requirements and time-to-certify create a narrow entry path for local health departments. Workforce shortage data not retrieved this session; verify with NEHA/NACCHO.

role_title: State natural resource district or corrections-camp manager
description: WA created Natural Resource Specialist 6 (2025-07-01) for district and corrections camp managers, combining land management, crew leadership and fire.
EGLE MUSTA analysts review UST cleanup fund claims and invoices: document-review work likely compressible by AI (judgment). Evidence of the role is retrieved; exposure is judged.

role_title: NEPA specialist / NEPA coordinator / interdisciplinary team leader
description: Shifts from authoring EAs/EISs under one CEQ rulebook to running agency-specific procedures (some now handbooks), choosing the level of review, managing statutory page and time limits, documenting CEs, supervising applicant-prepared documents, and keeping a defensible record. Fewer EISs and more CE determinations are likely where CEs expanded (USDA plan-level CE; Reclamation CE consolidation).

role_title: Junior environmental document writer / NEPA analyst (consulting and agency)
description: First drafts of resource sections, literature and legal comparisons, and comment binning were how juniors learned review. These are the tasks AI now handles (DraftNEPABench: 1-5 hours saved per subsection; CommentNEPA in production) and the tasks v1 called S. Without a designed substitute (supervised validation work, mock hearings, record audits), the pipeline to senior NEPA judgment thins.

Moves from reading and coding comments to validating AI groupings, finding unique substantive comments, and drafting legally adequate responses. Very large dockets (371,657 comments on the 2026 Roadless proposal; more than 220,000 on WOTUS) make AI triage unavoidable. If SPEED passes, unique comments would decide who can sue.

role_title: State permit writer (NPDES, Title V, CWA 404 assumed programs)
description: Must manage the oversight relationship and the federal predicates of delegated authority, adapt to unsettled WOTUS jurisdiction, and produce structured permit data for digital systems. The Florida 404 reversion (2026) shows that program authority, and so the workforce built on it, can vanish when federal predicate actions fail.

role_title: Good Neighbor / partnership agreement program manager
description: 540 Forest Service GNAs in FY2025 (426 with 39 states). Counties and Tribes can now retain revenue, recreation GNAs began January 2026, Colorado extended state GNA authority to DOI agencies in 2026, and 20-year agreements are proposed. State forestry agencies and counties need staff who design agreements, administer timber sales and manage retained revenue.

role_title: County natural resources / public lands coordinator (cooperating-agency liaison)
description: Counties can hold GNAs and retain revenue. Under DOI procedures they must justify cooperating-agency participation, which bureaus can deny with reasons. SPEED would create 'local cooperating agency' status. County staff become intergovernmental negotiators, not only commenters.

role_title: Tribal natural resources / environmental program director
description: New revenue-retaining GNA authority, uncertain federal support for co-stewardship (EO 14112 rescinded 2025-03-14), and consultation duties that persist while NEPA accelerates. Tribal directors act as sovereign regulators, rights-holders and agreement partners at once. TN must validate this description.

role_title: Permitting technology product owner / permitting data steward
description: Created by the 2025 Presidential Memorandum, the CEQ Action Plan (agency adoption within 90 days) and data standard v1.2. Bridges statute and procedure with BPMN/DMN screening logic, structured documents and dashboards. The ePermit Act would make it statutory. It is SC-primary because the product is a lawful process, with heavy DC.

role_title: Corporate climate disclosure / regulatory affairs manager
description: Federal disclosure is receding (SEC rescission proposed 2026-05-29; GHGRP cuts proposed), while California SB 253 reporting starts 2026-11-10 and the EU CSRD continues with narrower scope. The role splits into multi-jurisdiction compliance strategy (statecraft) and emissions accounting and assurance (data craft).

role_title: ESA consultation biologist (Services and action agencies) / HCP negotiator
description: The harm rescission (effective 2026-09-12), the end of the blanket 4(d) rule, the 4(b)(2) exclusions rule and pending section 7 changes alter what is negotiated in incidental take statements, HCPs and 4(d) rules. Litigation was noticed on 2026-07-15, so practice must hold up under either outcome.

Jurisdictional determinations remain unsettled (2025 proposal, 2026 supplemental proposal, no final rule), so specialists must also know state and Tribal wetland law for waters outside federal jurisdiction.

With the federal GHG endangerment finding rescinded, air districts are litigating (Bay Area AQMD v. EPA, filed 2026-04-16) and leaning on state authority. District staff need litigation-support, rulemaking and coalition statecraft that v1 does not cover (6.7.5 sits under EH&J).

role_title: Applicant-side environmental review / permitting manager (energy, infrastructure, mining sponsors)
description: New tools: paying for Sec. 112 acceleration, preparing EAs and EISs for agency evaluation, adopting CEs, and dealing with ESA and Section 106 as the new critical path. The role grows in scope and moves closer to the agency's own work.

role_title: Entry-level policy analyst (agency, NGO, think tank)
description: v1 classifies policy literature review (6.4.1 T1) and legal comparison (6.1.1 T2) as substitution. The analyst ladder loses its first rung unless entry work is redesigned around validating, synthesizing for a specific decision, and briefing.

Seven County's deference and limits on vacatur reduce litigation leverage. SPEED would add a 150-day limitations period and a unique-comment standing rule. Advocacy shifts toward early engagement, durable comment craft, state and local venues, and statutes outside NEPA (ESA notice letters).

role_title: Third-party neutral / environmental mediator and facilitator
description: Agency demand for required public process falls (no public involvement required for CEs and EAs under DOI), but contested decisions and partnership agreements need neutral convening for legitimacy. The net direction is unknown. The status of the federal environmental conflict resolution program (Udall Foundation) was not verified this session.

USDA's 2026 procedures can categorically exclude plan amendments and revisions, and the 2026 objection rule shortens windows. Planner statecraft moves from EIS management to component drafting, objection resolution and monitoring commitments (consistent with OpenLMP's 58,544 plan components as demand signal).

Leads interdisciplinary NEPA/permit teams where AI drafts, searches and sorts comments; owns scoping judgment, prompt/specification, validation and accountable sign-off; defends the record under shorter deadlines and a 150-day limitations period if SPEED Act passes. Needs FS-C01, FS-C03, FS-C09 plus core 6.1.4. Entry paths: NEPA specialists (0028/0401), consulting PMs, CAREP-type credential holders.

role_title: Environmental model risk and AI assurance officer
description: Inventories AI uses, classifies high-impact uses (OMB M-25-21), sets test and monitoring requirements, audits vendor models used in permitting, enforcement targeting and monitoring. Needs FS-C02, FS-C10, 7.1.4. Entry paths: data scientists (1560) with regulatory exposure, QA/QC leads, auditors; career move for senior analysts displaced by drafting automation.

Verification shifts from document audit to auditing remote-sensing models, sensor data and dynamic baselines, plus targeted field calibration; must quantify assessor variability. Needs FS-C07, FS-C08, 6.6.1. Entry paths: foresters, field ecologists and GHG accountants adding model-audit skills.

Designs and maintains field plots, labelled reference sets and regional validation for EO foundation models, dMRV and AI classifiers; decides where models are fit for use. Needs FS-C04, 2.2.3, 2.2.5, 4.1.1. Entry paths: field technicians and inventory crews (0404/0462), FIA-type programs; protects a field-craft ladder by giving it a data-craft destination.

24/7 fusion of satellite detection (FireSat-class), cameras, weather and fuels into decision support for initial attack, resource ordering and public warning; outside NWCG incident-only intelligence. Needs FS-C05, 4.3.4, 2.1.2. Entry paths: fire crews with GIS skills, IMETs, geospatial analysts, utility situational-awareness staff.

Evaluates, pilots, procures and scales detection, AI and aviation technologies; manages vendor data rights and training. Precedent: CAL FIRE Office of Wildfire Technology R&D. Needs FS-C10, FS-C09. Entry paths: fire management officers, aviation and IT program managers.

Owns a case-management or AI review product inside an agency: user research with reviewers, backlog, data-standard compliance, change management. Driven by CEQ data standard and Permitting Innovation Center; FAS/EPIC called for product managers. Needs FS-C09. Entry paths: experienced reviewers moving into product roles; digital-service staff gaining domain depth.

role_title: Drone and robotic operations program lead
description: Runs BVLOS fleets, airspace compliance, data pipelines and safety management once Part 108 lands; precursor is local drone-as-first-responder programs (>1,000 agencies on waivers). Needs FS-C06, 4.5.4, 4.4.1. Entry paths: UAS pilots, aviation managers, survey crews.

Maintains data assimilation, validation under nonstationarity, uncertainty communication and governance (incl. data sovereignty) for operational twins of watersheds, forests or fire. Currently research-stage. Needs FS-C11, 2.7.3. Entry paths: modelers, hydrologists, research-to-operations scientists.

role_title: Environmental AI evaluation and training expert
description: Domain experts design realistic multi-step environmental tasks and grading rubrics used to train and evaluate AI agents (posting requires 3+ years at agency/consultancy; ~USD 1,150-1,450 per task). Needs FS-C17. Entry paths: experienced and recently displaced agency and consulting staff. Ambivalent: builds the systems that may substitute for entry work.

Negotiates and administers co-stewardship, Good Neighbor, 638 and state-based leadership agreements as management devolves; tracks obligations, funding and performance. Needs FS-C14, 6.5.1, 6.5.3. Entry paths: Tribal liaisons, grants and agreements specialists (1109), state forestry staff.

Runs structured tacit-knowledge elicitation, paired work and field-walk capture with departing experts; maintains communities of practice and re-employed annuitant programs. Needs FS-C12, 7.2.2. Entry paths: senior practitioners, training officers, knowledge managers.

role_title: Corporate GHG and nature data controller
description: Owns auditable Scope 1-3 and nature-related data for SB 253 (first reports 10 Nov 2026), ESRS and ISSB-aligned regimes; narrative reporting roles shrink as standards simplify and templatize. Needs FS-C18, 6.6.1. Entry paths: accountants, environmental compliance staff, EHS managers.

Assesses business dependencies and impacts on biodiversity, structures nature-credit and blended-finance deals; legitimized by IPBES Business and Biodiversity Assessment. Needs 6.6.2, 6.6.4, FS-C07. Entry paths: ecologists with finance training, ESG analysts.

Helps communities and small jurisdictions translate hazard data into funded adaptation options as federal technical assistance thins and data moves to NGOs. Needs FS-C16, 1.5.3. Entry paths: planners, extension agents, floodplain managers, AmeriCorps alumni.

Coordinates volunteer data with AI-assisted identification and automated QA; becomes a capacity substitute where paid monitoring is cut. Needs 5.4.4, FS-C08. Entry paths: educators, volunteer managers, field technicians. Confirm with posting data.

role_title: Administrative record and AI provenance specialist
description: Assembles litigation-ready records documenting which analyses were AI-assisted, data lineage and human review, under shorter limitations periods and 'substantive comment' rules. Needs FS-C03. Entry paths: paralegals, records managers, NEPA coordinators. Speculative until courts rule on AI-assisted records.

The P-position learning substrate (drafting, literature and document review, comment coding) is being automated first in consulting and agencies; v1 rates CLD 'Highest' on 6.1.1, 6.1.2, 6.4.1, 6.4.4. Without redesign, few will reach review-and-certify competence.

role_title: Conservation corps, internship and seasonal crew member
description: Paid internships -43.8% and AmeriCorps -42% in 2025 postings; USD 400m AmeriCorps cuts; this is the main entry ladder for field craft and a diversity pipeline.

BLM, NPS, BIA, FWS fire programs consolidating into the U.S. Wildland Fire Service (~4,000 permanent staff); USFS merger blocked pending feasibility study. Qualification and classification will be redesigned.

role_title: Utility fire-weather and wildfire risk specialist
description: Utility situational-awareness centers hire meteorologists for fire-weather forecasting, PSPS and model development (WRF, Python); competes with NWS/IMET and agency talent.

As USFS moves to state-based leadership models and partners take on management, state staff need federal-equivalent NEPA, sale-prep, consultation and agreement competencies without federal training pipelines.
EO embeddings and AI classification compress routine mapping and change detection; work shifts to validation, labels and interpretation (v1 2.1.1 and 2.1.2 modal Ac; 2.1.2 S-trajectory).
AI theme and sentiment sorting of comments already in consulting use; remaining human work is judging substantive comments and responding.
Species ID moves to automated classifiers and molecular assays; analyst role becomes sample design, chain of custody and classifier QA (v1 2.6.2 modal V; 1.6.2 S-trajectory).
Data-centre and generation siting adds water-rights, transmission and community-consent review load to environmental and Tribal staff.
Federal EJ positions selectively left on leave or eliminated; capacity migrating to state programs and community organizations (refugia).

Employment has shifted from BIA to Tribal governments under self-determination: 1,479 BIA vs 775 Tribal employees in 1991; 436 BIA vs 1,394 Tribal in 2019, with total staffing down. Tribal governments are now the main employer of trust-forest professionals.

BIA agency forestry capacity has eroded: Yakama Agency failed to fill dozens of vacant forestry positions for over a decade and completed one timber sale in a year on about 650,000 forested acres; IFMAT IV reports harvests at about 50% of allowable levels and difficulty hiring permanent staff due to funding uncertainty.

role_title: Tribal wildland fire staff (FMO, fuels, crews) under BIA programs
description: BIA fire moved into the U.S. Wildland Fire Service (launched Jan 12 2026; personnel moves from Feb 8 2026); SO 3443 directs standardized fire position descriptions and joint AD hiring; FY2027 request funds 640 Tribal wildland fire FTEs and permanent pay increases; Tribes decide whether to adopt pay reform. Congress did not endorse the consolidation in FY2026 appropriations.

role_title: Tribal liaison / Office of Tribal Trust staff (USWFS)
description: DOI proposes an Office of Tribal Trust reporting to the USWFS Director to handle consultation, co-stewardship, ISDEAA assumption and retrocession; Tribes asked for Tribal liaison positions with real decision authority, staffed early, complementing rather than replacing local staff.

role_title: Year-round Tribal fire position combining suppression, fuels and post-fire recovery
description: Tribes asked for year-round positions combining suppression, fuels and recovery work, and for recurring compactable fuels funding instead of project-by-project awards; the FY2027 request describes building a year-round professional workforce.

Recognition of Tribally led cultural burning is growing (Tribes requested cultural burning protocols and reduced barriers; California's 2021 forest strategy created a grant program for Tribal cultural burning). The role and its qualifications are defined by Tribes; EMST should record that the role exists and how partners support it, not define its content.

role_title: Tribal environmental director / coordinator (GAP-funded multi-media generalist)
description: FY2026 GAP (about 520 awards, minimum $75k) emphasizes capacity to implement delegated federal programs, EPA-Tribal Environmental Plans, intergovernmental collaboration, and solid and hazardous waste service delivery, with climate and EJ language absent; regional notices emphasize CWA 106 monitoring strategies and PFAS. Small staffs cover many media, so the role is a generalist with regulatory, grants and technical duties.

role_title: Tribal environmental science and monitoring staff funded by competitive federal grants
description: 2025 terminations and holds hit Tribal science positions: Northwestern Band of the Shoshone Nation lost a funded line for Bear River watershed restoration (over $6M in awards since 2023); an Alaska Tribe's salmon and wildlife monitoring network funding was at risk; an Alaska Tribal organization had $130M on hold. Competitive-grant-funded positions are the least stable entry path.

role_title: Native student intern / early-career pipeline programs
description: A paid New England Native student internship program was put on indefinite hold in 2025; partners withdrew from a climate program under the anti-DEI order. BIA Pathways continues to place interns, some of whom move into Tribal environmental jobs (e.g., an intern now Environmental Protection Department Manager for the Northfork Rancheria). ED-DOI-DOL interagency agreements (consulted Feb 2026) may move program administration; effects not yet known.

role_title: Tribal forester hired under preference from another discipline
description: IFMAT IV (C4): Tribal and Indian preference increased Native foresters but some hires come from other disciplines, complicating NASP certification; recommends a forester 'boot camp' and NASP access. NASP classes continue for BIA and Tribal foresters (Class 19 Module 2 at Oregon State; Class 20 applications closed Dec 2025).

role_title: Federal land management planner (Tribal coordination duties)
description: Plans written under the 2012 Planning Rule carry about 27 Tribal coordination touchpoints per 1,000 components versus about 10 in 1982-rule plans, and Indigenous/Tribal terms rise from 8.5 to 26.2 per 1,000; examples include treaty-rights desired conditions, first-foods guidelines and a monitoring indicator counting receipt of traditional ecological knowledge (Ashley 2024 MON-TRIBE-01). State plans carry far fewer (about 4 per 1,000).

role_title: Federal cultural resource / Section 106 specialist and THPO counterpart
description: The ACHP voted 16-5 on July 24 2026 to advance a rewrite of 36 CFR 800 (pending OIRA; not yet published as of mid-Aug 2026): consultation redefined as seeking and considering views; agency Memoranda of Decision replace agreements; THPO involvement reduced; noncompact natural features excluded from historic property definition. Federal specialist work shifts toward agency-prepared consolidated reports; Tribal THPOs face more advocacy and legal work to be heard. Proponents expect faster permitting; final rule expected 2027.

Agreements grew to about 400 by Dec 2024 under S.O. 3403; in 2025 EO 14112 was rescinded and in July 2026 the Bears Ears Commission, the first Tribal co-management commission of its kind, was eliminated by proclamation. Whether S.O. 3403 and bureau co-stewardship policies remain in force was not verified; the direction of travel for federal-side co-stewardship roles is down, while Tribal-side roles may persist under Tribal authority.

role_title: Tribal fire program fiscal / reimbursement specialist
description: Tribes report large federal reimbursement backlogs (about $8.6M owed to the Santa Ynez Band of Chumash Indians since 2019; about $3M to the Karuk Tribe), which demands grants, invoicing and federal cost-recovery expertise inside Tribal programs; DOI proposes a centralized fire payment center.

role_title: Federal staff who participate in Tribal consultation or receive Indigenous knowledge
description: Formal competency prerequisites now exist in policy: DOI 2022 consultation policy requires training before participating in consultation; 301 DM 7 requires training on IK policy before engaging and FPIC before receiving IK; NPS DO 71C commits to reviewing positions, identifying required competencies (including co-stewardship and Indigenous knowledge) and performance standards. CRS (Sep 2026) finds natural-resource agency consultation policies generally remain in effect; IK policy status in 2026 unverified.

role_title: Tribal fish and wildlife / natural resource staff (treaty fisheries, inter-Tribal commissions)
description: Not assessed in depth: the web-search budget for this run was exhausted before inter-Tribal fisheries commissions (e.g., CRITFC, GLIFWC, NWIFC) and NAFWS workforce sources could be read. Plans show treaty fishing/hunting accommodation demands (NWFP ACS American Indian Uses; Nez Perce-Clearwater). Treat as an open evidence gap, not a finding.
